items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I arrived at that title from Joe Louis, that did this shuffling, you know, with his feet in prize-fighting.

ctx.x: with him, like the great and late Omer Simeon, you know. That's the saxophone player that was in my band, and he was an excellent reader and later on he became famous for his dixieland work on clarinet. And I made a few arrangements for Earl because he was broadcasting like one of those same things in New York. And I was working in Chicago at the time, and I made quite a few things for him because the guys like Walter Fuller, who used to sing "Rosetta," would be featured in that band as a trumpet player, used to…
So I made a thing for him, and I called it "Shufflin' Joe," and I arrived at that title from Joe Louis, that did this shuffling, you know, with his feet in prize-fighting.
